title: The relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and young patients after PCI: the mediating role of fear of disease progression
authors: Yuxin Li; Xiaoli Zhong; Tianxia Zhao; Ping Dai; Junrong Yang; Yuting Fan; Jijun Wu; Lin He
abstract: Objective This study aims to investigate the mediating role of fear of disease progression in the relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and young patients after PCI, providing a theoretical basis for developing targeted interventions to improve health promotion behaviors in this population. Methods This cross-sectional study employed convenience sampling. Between April and October 2024, 265 middle-aged and young patients who underwent PCI were surveyed in the cardiovascular department of a Grade A tertiary hospital in Sichuan Province, China. Data collection utilized questionnaires on general information, the Health-Promoting Lifestyle Scale, the Perceived Social Support Scale, and the Fear of Disease Progression Scale. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 software for descriptive analysis, univariate analysis, correlation analysis, and multivariate stratified regression analysis. Mediating effect analysis was conducted using Model 4 in the Process v4.1 plugin. Results The mean health-promoting behaviors score among middle-aged and young patients after PCI was (88.09 ± 9.98) points. Correlation analysis revealed that perceived social support was negatively correlated with fear of disease progression ( r = −0.478, p < 0.01) and positively correlated with health-promoting behaviors ( r = 0.715, p < 0.01). Fear of disease progression was negatively correlated with health-promoting behaviors ( r = −0.610, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed that fear of disease progression mediated the relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors, with an effect size of 0.068. This mediation accounted for 13.9% of the total effect. Conclusion There is still room for further improvement in health-promoting behaviors among middle-aged and young patients following PCI. There is a significant correlation among perceived social support, fear of disease progression, and health-promoting behaviors, with fear of disease progression partially mediating the relationship between perceived social support and health-promoting behaviors. This study elucidates the interrelationships among these three factors and their underlying mechanisms, suggesting that clinicians may develop personalized rehabilitation management plans by integrating patients’ social support status with their psychological characteristics regarding disease-related fears. This approach offers new insights for optimizing health behavior management in middle-aged and young patients following PCI.

title: Quality standards for the diagnosis and management of ATTR and AL amyloidosis: a nominal group technique study
authors: Laura Piera Obici; Thibaud Damy; Lucía Galán; William Edward Moody; João R. Agostinho; Carys Barton; Catarina Campos; Giovanni D’Alessio; Keith Dares; Maike Franziska Dohrn; Nowell Fine; David Gregory; Emmanuel Jammes; Katharine McIntosh; Tomás Ripoll‐Vera; Ali Yılmaz; Isabel Ritchie; Giovanni Palladini
abstract: Background Transthyretin (ATTR) and immunoglobulin light-chain (AL) amyloidosis are progressive conditions that can have debilitating effects on people. Delayed diagnosis and variable access to high-quality care continue to affect quality of life and prognosis. Clear and ambitious quality standards could drive consistent care and improve outcomes.Methods A modified nominal group technique was used to develop consensus-based quality standards for the diagnosis and management of ATTR and AL amyloidosis. Eighteen experts participated, including patient representatives and clinicians from high-income, publicly funded health systems in Europe and Canada. Each quality standard was paired with at least one measurable indicator to support implementation and monitoring.Results A total of 29 provisional statements were generated, with consensus achieved on eight quality standards. These span the full care pathway and emphasise the need for timely, person-centred and interdisciplinary care. Twenty accompanying indicators were developed.Conclusion This is the first comprehensive set of consensus-based quality standards for ATTR and AL amyloidosis care. They provide a practical and aspirational framework to guide quality improvement across health systems. Adoption of these standards could improve early diagnosis, equitable access to treatment, and quality of life. Future research may explore their feasibility and adaptation for other health system settings.

title: A whole-blood transcriptomic analysis of shared molecular mechanisms between subclinical atherosclerosis and hypothyroidism in women
authors: Emiliana María Torres; Diego Alejandro Raffo; Mariana Lorena Tellechea
abstract: Introduction Hypothyroidism (HT) is clinically associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, yet the shared molecular mechanisms underlying subclinical atherosclerosis (sAS) in hypothyroid patients remain poorly understood. This study aims to identify common transcriptomic signatures and regulatory axes between these two conditions. Methods We performed an integrated transcriptomic analysis of peripheral whole-blood datasets retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE176153 and GSE221615). To minimize sex-based biological bias, the analysis was restricted to female samples. Differential expression, functional enrichment, network topology, and transcription factor prediction were performed to identify shared differentially expressed genes (SDEGs) and candidate transcriptional regulators. The classification performance of selected pivotal SDEGs and predicted transcription factors was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Public transcriptomic data from myeloid-specific Tshr-knockout murine macrophages (GSE275079) were additionally examined to explore the myeloid context of TSH–TSHR signaling, followed by in vitro RT-qPCR validation in human THP-1 macrophages exposed to TSH and LPS. Results We identified 20 female-restricted SDEGs enriched in pathways related to B-cell proliferation and activation. Integration of functional enrichment, functional network analysis, and PPI topology highlighted six pivotal genes: BLK , CD19 , CD180 , TNFRSF13C , SPIB, and FCRLA . SPI1 and MEF2A were identified as key candidate regulators collectively targeting this gene set. Exploratory ROC analyses showed discriminatory capacity for several pivotal SDEGs and candidate transcription factors across the study cohorts, with some of these findings also observed in an external cohort of advanced atherosclerotic disease. Analysis of Tshr-knockout murine macrophage data revealed enrichment in lymphocyte and mononuclear cell proliferation pathways, alongside downregulation of Ifrd1 . In human THP-1 macrophages, TSH alone and in combination with LPS were associated with a significant downregulation of IFRD1 expression. Discussion These findings suggest a potential sex-specific immune-endocrine link between thyroid dysfunction and atherosclerotic disease, characterized by a shared transcriptomic axis converging on B-cell-associated pivotal genes and candidate transcriptional regulators. Exploratory myeloid analyses further identified TSH-associated downregulation of IFRD 1.

title: Surgical Reconstruction of Posterior Cricoid Injury Following Airway Management Resulting in Tracheoesophageal Fistula: A Case Report
authors: Min Young Shin; Chaewon Suh; Siyeon Jin; Jungirl Seok
journal: Korean Journal of Otorhinolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
abstract: Acquired tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF) in adults may arise from iatrogenic injury during airway management; in particular, hypopharyngeal-subglottic fistula (HSF) involving the cricoid is rare.We report a 61-year-old male who underwent repeated intubations and percutaneous tracheostomy for infective endocarditis.During recovery, aspiration led to the diagnosis of a high-level TEF with bilateral vocal fold paralysis (BVFP).Imaging 4 months after tracheostomy suggested posterior cricoid compromise, and surgery revealed fibrosis, loss of cricoid architecture, and a small posterior fistula.Open airway reconstruction using a laryngeal cleft-type multilayer closure with autologous graft achieved durable closure, preserved airway function, and enabled gradual decannulation without recurrence at 1 year.This case highlights that iatrogenic airway injuries can cause delayed posterior cricoid collapse with HSF and BVFP, and that multilayer reconstruction is an effective treatment in complex adult cases.

title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis
authors: Antonio De Vita; Marcello Covino; Francesco Mollo; Matteo Vumbaca; Chiara Napolitano; Saverio Tremamunno; Nello Cambise; Rosaria Natali; Marco Rossi; Tiziana Bove; Raffaele Vitiello; Giulio Maccauro; Francesco Franceschi; Carlo Trani; Francesco Burzotta; Gaetano Antonio Lanza
abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04–2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03–0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

title: Case Report: Refractory childhood-onset takayasu arteritis with digital clubbing and extensive supra-aortic and lower-limb arterial disease
authors: Fawzy Mazen Abunejma; Leen M. Jabari; Marah Nouredeen Hamad; Tamer O. Tamimi; Omair Bseiso; Hisham Aziz Dweik; Raed M. A. Isayed; Hanan Qunibi; Waleed Alzaro; Wasef Alhroub
abstract: Childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis is rare, and its early picture is often too vague to point at a large-vessel vasculitis. We report a 12-year-old girl who presented with 13 days of recurrent severe retrosternal chest pain and diffuse colicky abdominal pain, on a background of six months of exertional fatigue and painful swelling of the right fingertips, without fever, weight loss or night sweats. Examination showed bilateral digital clubbing, a right arm blood pressure below the 5th percentile with left arm and lower limb readings between the 50th and 90th percentiles, an absent right radial pulse, and weak brachial and right posterior tibial pulses. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 110 mm/h and C-reactive protein 82 to 93 mg/L. Computed tomography angiography showed mild concentric mural thickening of the aortic arch with severe stenosis of the right common and internal carotid arteries, near-occlusion of the right subclavian artery, moderate to severe brachiocephalic stenosis, moderate narrowing of the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries, and moderate stenosis of the right common and superficial femoral arteries. The abdominal aorta and its visceral branches were spared. She met the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES (Ankara 2008) classification criteria for childhood Takayasu arteritis, and the arterial distribution corresponds to Numano type IIa, together with peripheral lower-limb involvement that the Numano scheme does not cover. Disease progressed on intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, methotrexate, aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin, culminating in an 80% stenosis of the right common femoral artery. Adalimumab was started and later replaced by tocilizumab, after which the femoral peri-arterial inflammatory changes resolved on imaging and acute-phase reactants normalized. Blood pressure asymmetry, pulse deficits and the established stenoses persisted. This case suggests that normal inflammatory markers in childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis can coexist with fixed arterial damage, and that judgements about disease activity are better based on clinical findings and serial imaging together than on acute-phase reactants alone.

title: Temporal stability of femoral artery access localization in repeated digital subtraction angiography: clinical determinants and anatomical variability
authors: Yasin Taşkın; Sefa Erdi Ömür; Çağrı Zorlu; Cemal Köseoğlu; Yunus Emre Kuyucu
abstract: Aim: To evaluate the temporal stability of femoral artery access-site localization in patients undergoing repeated digital subtraction angiography (DSA) and to identify independent anatomical and procedural factors associated with instability in localization.Methods: This retrospective analytical study included 161 patients who underwent femoral artery access on multiple occasions for DSA or neurointerventional procedures between December 2020 and December 2024. Only patients who underwent repeated ipsilateral femoral access were included in the primary temporal stability analysis to avoid anatomical variation between limbs. Femoral artery puncture sites were fluoroscopically classified as being located over or outside the femoral head. Punctures outside the femoral head were further categorized as high or low punctures. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of localization instability.Results: The mean age was 56.25±14.42 years, and 54.2% of patients were male. The proportion of punctures located over the femoral head decreased from 78.9% during the initial access to 71.4% during repeat access. The proportion of punctures outside the femoral head increased from 21.1% to 28.6%, although this paired within-patient difference was not statistically significant. On multivariable analysis, BMI ≥25 kg/m², high femoral bifurcation, femoral artery calcification, increased skin-to-artery depth, smaller common femoral artery diameter, and absence of ultrasound guidance were independently associated with localization instability.Conclusion: Femoral artery access-site localization may vary across repeated DSA and endovascular procedures, even when ipsilateral access is used. Patient-specific reassessment of femoral anatomy and ultrasound-guided puncture may improve the reproducibility of access-site localization and procedural safety.

title: Progression rates of aortic stenosis in patients with calcific and rheumatic heart disease in Saudi Arabia
authors: Zeinelabdien Elsherif; Dania Elsherif; Amjad M. Ahmed; Husam Ismail Ardah; Fawaz Al-Mutairi; Safeah Almaghrabi; Futun Alanazi; Hind Alaqeel; Mashael Almohaimeed; Rana Alklaib; Jawza Aldakhil; Haifa Alturki
journal: American Heart Journal Plus Cardiology Research and Practice
abstract: Study objective Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is the most prevalent type of AS in developed countries. However, in developing countries, rheumatic heart disease (RHD), which has a low progression rate, remains the prevalent type. This study compared the progression rates of AS between the National Guard cohort and Western populations. Design This was a retrospective single-center cohort study. Participants Involving patients who underwent two echocardiographic examinations within an interval of at least 2 years. Main outcome measures Progression of aortic valve stenosis was assessed by measuring changes in the aortic valve area (AVA), peak aortic velocity, and mean aortic valve gradient. Results In total, 1669 patients (median follow-up: 6.9 years) were included in the analysis. The overall annual AVA progression rate was 0.074 ± 0.1 cm 2 /year (median: −0.061 cm 2 /year). Patients with RHD had lower progression rates than those without RHD (25%–35%; AVA: −0.036 [−0.042, −0.030] cm 2 /year). Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who exhibited calcific AS had the highest progression rate (AVA: −0.102 ± 0.096 cm 2 /year). The overall progression rate of AS for the National Guard cohort was lower across all groups compared with that in Western populations (AVA: −0.08 to 0.12 cm 2 /year). Conclusions Patients with ESRD who had calcific AS had the highest progression rate. Meanwhile, patients with RHD exhibited the lowest progression rate. The high prevalence of calcific AS in our study shows the importance of adherence to the American College of Cardiology/European Society of Cardiology guidelines for disease management.

title: Anticoagulation with Bivalirudin in a Case of Mitral Valve Replacement and Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting Requiring Prolonged Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Support: A Case of Emergency Surgery Due to Posterior Papillary Muscle Rupture
authors: Sedef Dündar; Cihan Yücel; Mücahit Ergin; Serkan Ketenciler
abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is an increasingly used support method in cases of refractory cardiopulmonary failure. However, due to the non-biological surfaces of the system and the inflammatory responses it induces, coagulation disorders may develop, necessitating meticulous anticoagulation management. At present, unfractionated heparin (UFH) is used as the standard; however, in complications such as heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), alternative agents may be required. We present the management of a 59-yearold male who developed acute mitral regurgitation due to posterior papillary muscle rupture and underwent emergency mitral valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting. Due to post-operative right ventricular failure, venoarterial ECMO support was initiated. On the 5 th day of ECMO, progressive thrombocytopenia and central catheter thrombosis occurred. With a high 4T score, HIT was suspected. UFH infusion was discontinued, and bivalirudin was initiated as an alternative anticoagulant. The anticoagulation process was monitored with activated clotting time and activated partial thromboplastin time, and therapeutic targets were successfully achieved without major bleeding or thrombotic complications. The patient was weaned off ECMO on day 15 and discharged in stable condition on post-operative day 74. This case demonstrates that bivalirudin is a safe and effective anticoagulant option in ECMO patients who develop HIT. In complex cases with heparin contraindications, bivalirudin plays an important role in individualized anticoagulation strategies.

title: Case Report: Impella CP-protected percutaneous coronary intervention of the last remaining vessel—a LIMA-to-LAD graft—complicated by no-reflow and rescued with a drug-coated balloon
authors: Fotios Toulgaridis; Stavros Tzortzis; Nikolaos Tsiamis; Konstantinos Sassalos; Nikolaos Karanikolas; Ioannis Mavrogenis; Anastasia N. Kitsiou; Georgios Triantis
abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of the last remaining conduit in a patient with severely impaired left ventricular function is among the most hazardous procedures in contemporary interventional cardiology, as any interruption of flow essentially constitutes a global ischemic insult. We describe a 77-year-old man, a former heavy smoker with an 80-pack-year smoking history, who had undergone three-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) 22 years previously. His medical history also included chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, severe heart failure with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25–30%, and severe mitral regurgitation (MR). At presentation, he had Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III angina and New York Heart Association class III symptoms. The most recent coronary angiogram, performed 6 months earlier, demonstrated chronic total occlusion (CTO) of both saphenous vein grafts, in addition to CTO of all three native epicardial coronary arteries. Thus, the left internal mammary artery (LIMA) graft to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) represented the sole functional conduit, directly perfusing the LAD territory and supplying the right coronary and circumflex territories through primarily septal and epicardial collaterals, respectively. The LAD displayed two sequential severe stenoses (≥80% each), one at the distal LIMA–LAD anastomosis and another further distally in the native vessel. In accordance with current coronary revascularization guidelines, the Heart Team recommended evaluation by cardiac surgeons. Two independent cardiothoracic surgeons declined redo CABG as a viable therapeutic option. Complex and high-risk indicated PCI (CHIP) was therefore considered the only feasible revascularization strategy. Additional hemodynamic support with percutaneous mechanical circulatory support (pMCS) was deemed necessary. Residual MR and arrhythmic risk, including the potential indication for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD), were planned to be reassessed 3 months after successful percutaneous revascularization. CHIP was performed under full hemodynamic support with a continuous-flow microaxial pump (Impella CP with SmartAssist) inserted via the left femoral artery, while coronary intervention was performed through the ipsilateral radial artery using a 6-F IMA guiding catheter. The lesions were successfully crossed with a workhorse wire, despite substantial technical difficulty and with the aid of a microcatheter; however, distal flow was immediately lost, and intracoronary nitroglycerin failed to restore it. Balloon angioplasty restored flow only partially, and a decision was made to proceed with stent implantation. However, stent delivery proved challenging, requiring a guide-extension catheter to be advanced deep into the LIMA body using the so-called ‘inchworming technique.’ Despite successful implantation of the first drug-eluting stent (DES) at the distal anastomotic lesion, a second DES could not be advanced to the more distal native LAD lesion, despite the use of multiple guidewires and supportive guiding-catheter strategies. Therefore, a drug-coated balloon (DCB) was used as a bailout strategy, immediately restoring TIMI grade 3 flow and leaving only a minor, non-flow-limiting type B dissection. Impella support was discontinued early because of access-related left lower-limb ischemia, and successful percutaneous hemostasis was achieved using a suture-based closure technique. Peak high-sensitivity troponin I, measured the following evening, was 10,800 pg/mL. The patient was discharged ambulatory on day 2 and remained asymptomatic at 3-month follow-up, when an ICD was implanted for primary prevention. This case illustrates the critical role of pMCS in maintaining hemodynamic stability when native coronary flow is lost during PCI of the last remaining conduit and highlights the value of DCB angioplasty as a bailout strategy when stent delivery is not feasible.

title: Anomalous Origin of the Left Coronary Artery from the Pulmonary Artery Beyond Infancy: Single-Center Experience of Clinical Spectrum and Surgical Outcomes
authors: Betül Çınar; Pelin Ayyıldız; Sertaç Haydın; Alper Güzeltaş
abstract: Objective: Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare and life-threatening congenital anomaly. While it typically manifests during early infancy, some patients remain asymptomatic or present later in childhood and adolescence due to well-developed intercoronary collaterals. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical spectrum, diagnostic features, and surgical outcomes of patients diagnosed with ALCAPA beyond infancy at our center. Methods: A retrospective review was conducted on 35 patients diagnosed with ALCAPA who underwent surgical treatment at our center between January 2012 and January 2025. Out of this cohort, 8 patients diagnosed beyond infancy (older than 12 months) were enrolled in this study to evaluate their clinical spectrum and surgical revascularization outcomes. Results: The age at diagnosis ranged from 2 to 21 years (median: 6.8 years), and all patients were female. Four patients (50%) were completely asymptomatic at presentation. Symptomatic presentations included exertional chest pain (n=1), recurrent vomiting and irritability (n=2), and sudden cardiac arrest with sustained ventricular arrhythmia (n=1). Electrocardiography (ECG) revealed characteristic ALCAPA patterns in 5 patients. Echocardiography demonstrated left ventricular (LV) and right coronary artery (RCA) dilation in all cases, with a mean RCA/aortic annulus ratio of 0.25. Baseline LV systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction: 30–45%) was observed in 4 patients. Surgical management consisted of direct coronary reimplantation (n=6) and the Takeuchi procedure (n=2). Mitral valve repair was performed in 2 patients with structural mitral anomalies. At a mean follow-up of 48 months, all patients were alive and asymptomatic, with full recovery of LV function and resolution of ECG abnormalities within 6–9 months postoperatively. Conclusion: ALCAPA must be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained LV dilation or mitral regurgitation across all pediatric age groups. Extensive collateral circulation can mask typical features, leading to atypical presentations or misdiagnosis. Prompt establishment of a dual-coronary system provides a satisfactoryprognosis and facilitates complete myocardial recovery.

title: Efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors on functional mitral regurgitation associated with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Charlie Kajo; Ahmed J. AlAraibi; Osama T Almutairi; Yaqeen H. Alaraibi; Abdullah A. Alibrahim; Yousef Kh A Almutawah; Salem  W. S. Alasfar; Mustafa  Wasif Ali; Aseel Hajjiri; Mohammad Alqaryuti; Abdullatif Alfehaid; Dana Z. Arekat
abstract: Background Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) commonly complicates heart failure (HF) and portends a poor prognosis. While sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve clinical outcomes and induce cardiac reverse remodeling in HF, their specific effect on FMR associated with HF severity remains uncertain. Methods Five databases were searched from inception to 21 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating SGLT2i in adult patients with HF and chronic FMR on background guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Primary outcomes were changes from baseline in effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) and regurgitant volume (RV). Secondary clinical outcomes included HF hospitalization and cardiovascular (CVS) death. Random-effects models were used. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Results Three RCTs involving 455patients were included. SGLT2i therapy was associated with a statistically significant reduction in EROA (MD −0.086 cm 2 , 95% CI −0.150 to −0.022) and RV (MD −10.87 mL, 95% CI −17.32 to −4.43), but substantial heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 72.5% and I 2 = 63.5%, respectively). On leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, statistical significance for both primary valvular outcomes was lost after omitting the EFFORT trial. The certainty of evidence was rated as low. Conclusion Addition of SGLT2i to GDMT was associated with reductions in FMR severity in pooled analyses; however, these findings were not robust in sensitivity analyses and are limited by low certainty of evidence. The apparent reduction in clinical events requires cautious interpretation due to event sparsity. These results should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory, warranting further validation in large-scale, prospective trials. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261462002 , PROSPERO CRD420261385207

title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Optimization in a Patient with Left Ventricular Non-Compaction Cardiomyopathy and Morbid Obesity.
authors: Arsalan Farhangee; Ion Mîndrilă
abstract: Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy (LVNC) is a rare myocardial disorder associated with heart failure and arrhythmias. Cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT) is an established treatment in patients with electrical dyssynchrony; however, achieving optimal response remains challenging in complex clinical scenarios. We report a 51-year-old male with LVNC, severe left ventricular dysfunction, morbid obesity, and recurrent atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. Despite initial improvement following CRT-D implan-tation, the patient developed progressive heart failure and recurrent ventricular tachycardia with high atrial arrhythmia burden, resulting in ineffective biventricular pacing. Following unsuccessful device optimisation strategies, a multidisciplinary decision was made to proceed with atrioventricular node ablation. This resulted in marked clinical and echocardiographic improvement, including recovery of left ventricular ejection fraction and symptomatic status. This case highlights the importance of ensuring adequate CRT delivery and demonstrates the pivot-al role of atrioventricular node ablation in patients with refractory atrial arrhythmias and suboptimal CRT response.

title: Acute Rheumatic Fever: A Five-year Tertiary Center Experience and Post-pandemic Trends
authors: Halise Zeynep Genç; Ali Nazım Güzelbağ; Burcu Çevlik; Şenay Çoban; Erkut Öztürk
journal: Journal of Updates in Cardiovascular Medicine
abstract: Objectives: Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) remains a significant cause of acquired heart disease among children in developing countries.This study aimed to evaluate the clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic characteristics; treatment approaches; and outcomes of ARF patients followed in a tertiary pediatric cardiology center and to explore differences between pandemic and post-pandemic periods. Materials and Methods:In this retrospective study, 122 patients diagnosed with ARF between May 2020 and August 2025 were analyzed.Using June 2022-when pandemic restrictions were eased-as a reference point, patients were divided into two groups: pandemic (n=41) and post-pandemic (n=81).Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, laboratory results, echocardiographic findings, treatments, and follow-up data were compared.Results: The mean age was 12.8±2.4years, and 62.3% of patients were male.The monthly number of cases increased from 1.58 to 2.13 in the post-pandemic period (p=0.048).Carditis was detected in 95% of patients, consistent with the tertiary referral profile of our study population.Although the rate of carditis was numerically higher in the post-pandemic period, the difference was not statistically significant (92% vs. 96%, p=0.403).Delayed presentation and elevated C-reactive protein levels were associated with carditis.Conclusion: An apparent increase in ARF cases was observed in the post-pandemic period; however, this likely reflects referral dynamics rather than a true epidemiological shift.Delayed presentation and increased inflammatory burden were associated with more severe cardiac involvement.

title: Fatal Cardiopulmonary Collapse, Bilateral Pleural Effusion, and Hypoxic En-cephalopathy in Neglected Severe Preeclampsia: A Case Report on Antenatal Surveillance and Access Gaps
authors: Yohanes Adam Elsoin
journal: Sriwijaya Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
abstract: Background: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal death worldwide. Where antenatal care (ANC) is absent and women lack health insurance, a hypertensive crisis can progress quickly to fatal multi-organ failure. Objective: To describe the clinical, hemodynamic, and laboratory course of fatal postpartum cardiopulmonary collapse after unmonitored severe preeclampsia. Methods: Single-patient case report (CARE guideline) at Dr. Saiful Anwar General Hospital, Malang, Indonesia. Clinical findings, serial laboratory values, arterial blood gases, echocardiography, ultrasonography, and chest radiography were recorded over nine days of intensive care and presented chronologically, with a descriptive comparison with the literature. Results: A 44-year-old uninsured primiparous woman with no ANC contacts had an emergency cesarean delivery for severe preeclampsia and left a secondary hospital against medical advice on postoperative day 2 because of financial hardship. At tertiary admission she was obtunded (Glasgow Coma Scale 13), with blood pressure 166/94 mmHg, hemoglobin 5.5 g/dL, and oliguria. Radiography showed large asymmetric bilateral pleural effusions (left ~1,250 mL) with compressive atelectasis; PaO₂/FiO₂ was 142.1 mmHg. Echocardiography showed concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, systemic vascular resistance 2,140 dyn·s/cm⁵, and E/e' 17.8 (PCWP ~24 mmHg). Despite mechanical ventilation, nicardipine, transfusions, and albumin, anuric renal failure (creatinine 5.20 mg/dL) and severe acidosis (pH 7.08, lactate 11.4 mmol/L) progressed, and cardiopulmonary arrest occurred on day 9. Conclusion: In this patient, unmonitored severe preeclampsia was followed by fatal cardiopulmonary collapse; hydrostatic overload and endothelial hyperpermeability are proposed mechanisms that were not directly measured. Emergency coverage at private obstetric facilities may help prevent premature discharge.

title: Ultrasound-guided haemodynamic profiling in haemodialysis patients: a single-centre prospective observational study protocol
authors: Samuel Larsen; Fabio Silvio Taccone; Alaín Le Moine; Filippo Annoni; Thomas E.R. Baudoux
abstract: Background Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) and chronic fluid overload are common and clinically important complications of maintenance haemodialysis, yet routine volume assessment remains imprecise. Multi-organ point-of-care ultrasound may provide a structured bedside assessment of cardiac reserve, pulmonary congestion and venous congestion. Methods and analysis This single-centre prospective observational cohort study will enrol approximately 60 adult patients receiving maintenance haemodialysis. Participants will undergo integrated ultrasound profiling immediately before and after dialysis at baseline and at 3, 6 and 9 months, with clinical outcomes followed for 12 months. The ultrasound protocol includes focused cardiac ultrasound, eight-zone lung ultrasound B-line quantification and a modified VEXUS assessment using inferior vena cava, hepatic vein and portal vein findings. Event-triggered intradialytic scans may also be performed for current IDH or suspected mismatch between the prescribed target weight and the best clinically tolerated weight. These examinations will not be pooled with scheduled assessments. A separate exploratory post-scan association analysis will include only scans completed while the patient is clinically stable, before the first same-session IDH and not in response to evolving current-session haemodynamic instability; the outcome is subsequent IDH before session end. Scans obtained during or after IDH or during evolving instability will be described only. The main descriptive objective is to characterise pre- and post-dialysis ultrasound-derived haemodynamic profiles and their within-session and longitudinal variability. The primary prespecified analysis for Objective 2 is an exploratory and non-confirmatory assessment of the within-patient association between pre-dialysis ultrasound parameters and same-session IDH using a scheduled-session case-crossover design. Secondary analyses include the separate event-triggered post-scan association analysis and an exploratory scheduled-session mixed-effects analysis. Event-triggered examinations will not contribute cases to the primary analysis. Exploratory objectives assess clinician-perceived usefulness and documented clinician-implemented prescription changes after delayed disclosure, without assessing clinical benefit. Ethics and dissemination The study has received ethics approval and will be conducted after written informed consent. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific meetings. Study registration https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN80571205 , identifier ISRCTN80571205.

title: Sex differences in clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a real-world cohort
authors: Miriam Estévez Táboas; Julio Echarte‐Morales; Ernesto Ruiz Golcher; Carlos Eduardo Sotomayor-Casillas; André González García; David Neuhalfen; Carla Iglesias-Otero; Elena García-Campos Losada; Nazaret Vázquez-Vázquez; David González Fernández; Hugo Prado Prado; Carmen Cuiñas Fariña; Andrés Antelo-Abeijón; Pablo Juan‐Salvadores; Rodrigo Estévez‐Loureiro; Jose A. Baz Alonso; Andrés Íñiguez; Victor Alfonso Jímenez-Díaz
abstract: Background Severe aortic stenosis is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases in the ageing population, and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an effective and less invasive therapeutic alternative. Anatomical, pathophysiological, and clinical differences between women and men may influence outcomes following the procedure. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sex and mortality and procedure-related complications after TAVI in a real-world cohort from the Vigo Health Area. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including 1,065 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent transfemoral TAVI between 2010 and 2023. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included bleeding, vascular complications, and new permanent pacemaker implantation. Time-to-event analyses were censored at 365 days; multivariable models used complete-case analysis. Results Women were older and had greater frailty and higher surgical risk scores than men. In-hospital and 1-year mortality were similar between sexes. Date-based 30-day mortality was 2.4% in men and 3.7% in women ( p = 0.225), and female sex was not independently associated with 30-day mortality after adjustment for age and STS score (adjusted OR 1.79, 95% CI 0.80–3.98; p = 0.154). Female sex was not independently associated with 1-year mortality (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.69–1.66; p = 0.772). Women had more bleeding in unadjusted analyses, but female sex was not significantly associated with any bleeding after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.92–2.81; p = 0.093). Male sex remained associated with higher odds of new permanent pacemaker implantation (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.03–2.17; p = 0.036). Conclusions Sex was not independently associated with short- or 1-year mortality after TAVI. Women had a higher unadjusted incidence of bleeding, whereas men had a higher incidence of new permanent pacemaker implantation that persisted after adjustment. These findings describe sex-related differences in procedural risk profiles but should be interpreted in the context of the observational design and the long study period.

title: Physicians’ perspectives on the impact of echocardiographic feedback: a qualitative interview study
authors: Anahita Behzadi; Hamed Tasdighi; Mohammad Mehdi Kiani; Amirhossein Fatahpour
abstract: Echocardiography is a widely used non-invasive imaging modality central to diagnosing and monitoring heart failure, valvular disease, congenital heart disease, and cardiomyopathy. However, inappropriate requests, variability in reporting quality, and limited follow-up of diagnostic performance remain concerns, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Audit and feedback is an established strategy for improving professional practice, but its application in echocardiography remains underdeveloped. This study aimed to explore physicians’ perspectives on how the impact of echocardiographic feedback on clinicians can be assessed in Iran. A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with an inductive approach and reflexive thematic analysis, following Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework. From August 2022 to September 2023, 30 semi-structured interviews were conducted with purposively sampled participants, including cardiologists, university faculty in statistics, biostatistics, and health sciences, health insurance experts, and physicians working in health insurance organizations and research centers. The average interview duration was 49 min. Data saturation was reached after interview 27. Transcripts were coded by two independent researchers using MAXQDA 20 software. Trustworthiness was ensured using Lincoln and Guba’s criteria. The analysis generated five main themes and twelve subthemes: (1) indications for performing echocardiography; (2) diagnosing a patient’s need for echocardiography; (3) components of a complete echocardiography report; (4) sample selection and control group; and (5) data recording and analysis method. Participants emphasized the importance of guideline-based indications, standardized reporting, a before-and-after design with a control group, and the Difference-in-Differences (DID) technique for evaluating feedback. A cross-cutting finding regarding the role of body habitus and thoracic morphology in echocardiographic interpretation was integrated into the framework. The findings provide a comprehensive qualitative basis for a proposed framework for future quantitative evaluation of echocardiographic feedback. Future studies should operationalize these domains into valid and reliable indicators and prospectively evaluate whether feedback can improve the appropriateness, quality, and consistency of echocardiographic practice.

title: Cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: insights from myocardial strain and renal Doppler assessment
authors: Ahmed Atef; Ahmed Fayed; Hemmat El- Haddad; Moataz Fathy; Heba El Deeb
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may be accompanied by subclinical cardiac and renal injury before overt disease appears. This study evaluated early cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early T2DM using myocardial strain imaging and renal Doppler assessment. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 180 participants: 60 with prediabetes, 60 with newly diagnosed T2DM (≤ 2 years), and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography were used to assess left ventricular (LV) function and left atrial (LA) mechanics. Renal vascular resistance was assessed using the Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI). Glycemic status and albuminuria were evaluated using fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance testing, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. RESULTS: Compared with controls, participants with prediabetes and T2DM showed early alterations in LV relaxation/filling indices and reduced LA strain. LV ejection fraction was modestly lower, while GLS became progressively less negative across the dysglycemic groups (p < 0.001), consistent with reduced longitudinal myocardial deformation. Renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI) were significantly increased in the dysglycemic groups. RRI correlated positively with E/e', linking higher renal vascular resistance with higher estimated LV filling pressure (r = 0.440, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Prediabetes and early T2DM were associated with subclinical abnormalities in myocardial mechanics and renal vascular indices despite preserved conventional cardiac and renal function. Myocardial strain and renal Doppler measures may provide complementary phenotypic information, but prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.

title: Totally endoscopic mitral valve replacement: reasons for non-feasibility of repair and 5-year outcomes
authors: Friedrich Sobik; Jonas Pausch; Xiaoqin Hua; Martin Beyer; Evelina Macius; Oliver Daniel Bhadra; Y. Alassar; Benjamin Kloth; Lenard Conradi; Hermann C. Reichenspurner; Simon Pecha; E. Girdauskas; Andreas Schaefer
abstract: Objectives Totally endoscopic mitral valve (MV) surgery is an established therapy for mitral regurgitation (MR) with high repair rates at experienced centers. In certain scenarios, however, repair is not feasible, necessitating chordal-sparing MV replacement. This study investigates the reasons for totally endoscopic MV replacement and reports 5-year outcomes. Methods Between 2012 and 2022, 1,037 consecutive patients underwent totally endoscopic MV surgery. Of those, 75 patients (7.2%) underwent chordal-sparing MV replacement. Preoperative characteristics, periprocedural data, and mid-term outcomes were retrospectively analyzed and compared to a 1:1 propensity score-matched repair group. Results After matching, baseline characteristics were balanced. Indications for MV replacement included sclerotic leaflets (28.0%), endocarditis (26.7%), MV stenosis (17.3%), failed repair attempt (17.3%), rheumatic disease (12.0%), and residual MR after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (7%). Cross-clamp and bypass times were similar. Re-thoracotomy occurred in 14.7% vs. 6.7%, while permanent pacemaker implantation occurred solely after replacement (16.0%). Low cardiac output rates were comparable (6.7% vs. 5.5%). Transvalvular gradients at discharge were higher after replacement ( p < 0.001). No paravalvular leakage was observed. In-hospital mortality was 4% vs. 0%. Five-year survival was 86.7% vs. 94.7%, and reintervention rates were similar (4.0% vs. 6.7%). Conclusion Totally endoscopic MV surgery at a high-volume center is infrequently associated with MV replacement. The main reasons included sclerotic leaflet pathology, MV stenosis, and endocarditis. Despite a higher comorbidity burden and residual baseline imbalance after matching, early and mid-term outcomes were acceptable. Totally endoscopic chordal-sparing MV replacement represents a safe and clinically effective treatment option for selected patients.

title: Case Report: Twelve-year longitudinal CMR follow-up in Becker muscular dystrophy–associated cardiomyopathy
authors: Mohd Imree Azmi; Masafumi Takafuji; Sven Plein
abstract: Cardiac involvement is an important cause of morbidity and mortality in Becker muscular dystrophy. Myocardial disease may progress despite relatively limited findings on conventional echocardiography, while cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) provides detailed assessment of ventricular function and myocardial tissue characteristics with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping and strain analysis. We report a case of 57 year-old man with genetically confirmed Becker muscular dystrophy who underwent CMR examinations 12 years apart. Follow-up imaging demonstrated progressive left ventricular remodelling, a decline in left ventricular ejection fraction and interval changes in the distribution and extent of myocardial fibrosis. This case provides a long-term within-patient comparison of Becker muscular dystrophy associated cardiomyopathy and illustrates the additional information provided by serial CMR in documenting progressive myocardial involvement over time.

title: Understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short Chinese videos on TikTok and Kwai: cross-sectional content analysis study
authors: Chen Chen; Xiaomeng Deng; Anting Xu; Siqi Luo; Qian Huang; Xiaohan Ma; Lunfang Xie
abstract: As one of the most prevalent malignant tumours of the digestive tract, colorectal cancer poses a serious threat to human health. While enterostomy procedures offer new hope for colorectal cancer patients, they also present new challenges to their ability to manage enterostomy care. Health information on enterostomy care is widely disseminated through short-video platforms such as TikTok and Kwai, which are popular for their strong dissemination power and interactive advantages. However, the understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short videos on these platforms had not been evaluated. This study evaluated the understandability and implementability of Chinese-language short videos on TikTok and Kwai about enterostomy care. From February to April 2025, we used the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Audiovisual Materials (PEMAT-A/V) to evaluate the understandability and implementability of 92 Chinese enterostomy care short videos (41 on TikTok and 51 on Kwai). We employed the Kruskal-Wallis H test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Spearman correlation analysis to explore factors potentially influencing comprehensibility and implementability. The results of the PEMAT-A/V evaluation showed that short videos on TikTok and Kwai about enterostomy care were more understandable (85.71 (71.76, 100.00) points) but poorer in implementability (66.67 (33.33, 66.67) points). Kwai was better than TikTok in terms of understandability and implementability. Short videos published by for-profit organisations (100.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), featuring live demonstrations (90.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), patient appearances (100.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), and background music (86.61 (81.37, 100.00) points) demonstrated superior understandability ( P < 0.05). Short videos featuring the patients themselves or nurses/enterostomy therapists/caregivers were more implementable ( P < 0.05). The understandability of enterostomy care short videos on TikTok and Kwai was generally satisfactory, though their implementability was suboptimal. To address issues identified during the quality assessment, targeted improvement strategies are proposed from the perspectives of creators and social media platforms. These aim to enhance both the understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short videos, thereby increasing their utility for audiences and providing a reference for creating health science popularisation short videos.

title: What are the indications and contraindications for using the Sapien M3 transcatheter device for mitral valve replacement?
authors: Tripdatabase
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The Sapien M3 device is indicated for patients with severe mitral regurgitation who cannot undergo surgery or TEER, with specific anatomical considerations. Contraindications include poor anatomy and unfavorable valve conditions.

title: Relation of serum electrolytes and left ventricular functions in patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI
authors: Leila Mohammadian; Farshad Zare; Hadi Haddadi; Shideh Roshani; Mostafa Naghdian; Sevda Ebrahimzadeh Fayazi; Masoumeh Alizadeh; Farinaz Amirikar; Ahmad Separham; Elnaz Javanshir; Erfan Banisefid
abstract: Electrolyte disturbances are common in STEMI patients. However, the association between admission serum electrolyte levels and echocardiographic findings after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the relationship between serum electrolyte levels, echocardiographic parameters, angiographic findings, and ST-segment resolution (STR) in patients with first anterior STEMI. In this observational study, 138 patients with first anterior STEMI undergoing PPCI were enrolled. Admission serum sodium, potassium, magnesium, total calcium, and ionized calcium levels were measured. Before hospital discharge, transthoracic echocardiography was performed to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), regional wall motion abnormality index (RWMAI), and left ventricular end-systolic volume index (LVESVI). Angiographic findings and STR were also assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was performed after adjustment for age and sex. Results at an exploratory level, lower serum potassium was associated in age- and sex-adjusted analyses with reduced LVEF (aOR = 2.984, 95% CI: 1.285–6.926; P = 0.011) and increased RWMAI (OR = 3.103, 95% CI: 1.338–7.196; P = 0.008); and patients with ionized calcium ≥ 1.05 mmol/L demonstrated significantly greater STR than those with lower levels ( P = 0.028). Serum sodium, magnesium, total calcium, and ionized calcium were not significantly associated with echocardiographic parameters. After Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, none of the observed associations remained statistically significant. Admission lower serum potassium is suggested to be associated with impaired left ventricular systolic function and more extensive RWMAI in patients with first anterior STEMI undergoing PPCI. However, these associations should be considered exploratory, particularly given the multiple electrolyte-outcome comparisons and the lack of statistical significance after Bonferroni correction.

title: Investigation of the relationship between heart rate measured automatically at different time intervals using the 3M littmann 3200 electronic stethoscope and heart rate measured by electrocardiography
authors: Ömer Aydın
journal: Journal of Advances in VetBio Science and Techniques
abstract: Cardiac auscultation is an indispensable method in the examination of cats. With a traditional stethoscope, heart murmurs, gallop rhythms, and heart rate (HR) may not always be accurately assessed because of ambient noise interference. However, electronic stethoscopes (ESs) provide more uniform and amplified acoustic signals, allowing more accurate identification of physiological and pathological heart sounds during auscultation. The aim of this study was to determine the agreement, differences, and correlation between HR automatically measured using a 3M Littmann 3200 ES over 15-, 30-, and 60-second intervals and HR obtained by electrocardiography (ECG) in 34 healthy cats of various breeds, ages, and sexes. To this end, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Bland–Altman, and Spearman’s correlation analyses were performed. ICC analysis showed moderate agreement between ECG and ES at the 15- and 60-second measurement intervals (r = 0.661, P < 0.001; r = 0.700, P < 0.001, respectively), whereas the 30-second interval demonstrated higher agreement (r = 0.812, P < 0.001). According to Bland-Altman analysis, 30-second HR measurements by ES showed the closest agreement with ECG (bias = 5.03; 95% limits of agreement = -34.34 to 44.40), compared to 15 seconds (bias = 9.41; -48.34 to 67.16) and 60 seconds (bias = 9.06; -41.88 to 59.99). In conclusion, this study demonstrates that 30-second measurements obtained with the 3M Littmann 3200 ES provide heart rate measurements comparable to those obtained by ECG in healthy cats.

title: Adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection incidence and mortality: results from the UK Biobank, the J-SHC study and a meta-analysis of cohort studies
authors: Alison Dillman; Yoichiro Otaki; M.R. Sánchez-Pérez; Momina Yawar Irfan Khan; Makoto Hibino; Tsuneo Konta; Kunihiro Yamagata; Shouichi Fujimoto; Kazuhiko Tsuruya; Ichiei Narita; Masato Kasahara; Yugo Shibagaki; Kunitoshi Iseki; Toshiki Moriyama; Masahide Kondo; Koichi Asahi; Tsuyoshi Watanabe; Tetsu Watanabe; Masafumi Watanabe; Dagfinn Aune
abstract: Abstract Few studies have investigated the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection and data is lacking on adiposity measures other than body mass index (BMI). We analyzed the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection in the UK Biobank, and the Japan Specific Health Checkups (J-SHC) Study, and conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to clarify the associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. The analytical cohorts included 496,255 participants in the UK Biobank and 630,841 participants in the J-SHC Study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. PubMed and Embase were searched for relevant studies up to February 27, 2026. Random effects models were used to calculate summary relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. In the UK Biobank and J-SHC, there were 371 and 105 aortic dissections during 12.3 and 4 years follow-up, respectively. In the UK Biobank, positive associations (HRs, 95% CIs) were observed between high BMI (1.54, 1.01–2.37, p trend =0.01), waist circumference (1.82, 1.27–2.60, p trend =0.001), hip circumference (1.77, 1.25–2.50, p trend <0.001), waist-to-height ratio (1.88, 1.30–2.70, p trend =0.10), and fat mass (1.36, 0.97–1.91, p trend =0.02) and aortic dissection risk, but no clear association was observed for waist-to-hip ratio (1.28, 0.90–1.81, p trend =0.08) and body fat percentage (1.09, 0.77–1.54, p trend =0.53). In the J-SHC Study, higher BMI (2.36, 0.98–4.84, p trend =0.018), waist circumference (2.26, 1.18–4.60, p trend =0.003), and waist-to-height ratio (2.61, 1.27–5.92, p trend =0.009) were positively associated with aortic dissection mortality. Five cohort studies were included in the meta-analysis on BMI and aortic dissection (2007 cases and 4,962,288 participants). The summary RR per 5 kg/m 2 increment in BMI was 1.09 (1.00-1.20, I 2 = 43%), per 10 cm increment in waist circumference was 1.21 (1.05–1.40, I 2 = 50%, n = 2), and per 0.1 unit increment in waist-to-height ratio was 1.32 (1.08–1.61, I 2 = 39%, n = 2). These findings provide evidence for a positive association between both general and abdominal adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection, with the strongest associations observed for high waist-to-height ratio. Although further large-scale studies are warranted for confirmation, these findings suggest avoiding excess weight may be an important strategy for the prevention of aortic dissection.

title: Biochemically supported diagnosis of Fabry disease in a young adult with unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy: a diagnostic challenge
authors: Noor Mohd Firdaus Othman; Hamizah Idrus; Sofwatul Mukhtaroh Nasohah; Ros Hamieza Mohd Yusoff; Siti Salbiah Norazan; Afif Ashari
abstract: Fabry disease (OMIM #301500) is a rare X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the GLA gene, resulting in deficient activity of α-galactosidase A. This enzymatic defect leads to lysosomal glycosphingolipid accumulation and progressive multisystem dysfunction. The clinical manifestations are variable and non-specific, which may delay diagnosis. We report a 29-year-old Malay man who presented with recurrent palpitations, exertional chest pain, dyspnoea and fatigue. The physical examination was unremarkable, and there was no known relevant family history. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated significant concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with markedly reduced native myocardial T1 values. No significant coronary artery abnormalities were identified, raising suspicion of an infiltrative or metabolic cardiomyopathy. Plasma α-galactosidase A activity was markedly reduced at 0.3 nmol/mL/h (reference interval, 2.0–10.0 nmol/mL/h), which, together with the compatible cardiac imaging findings, strongly supported a diagnosis of Fabry disease, although molecular confirmation was unavailable. This case highlights a cardiac-predominant presentation strongly supportive of Fabry disease in a young Malaysian adult without documented classical extracardiac manifestations or a known relevant family history. It underscores the importance of considering Fabry disease in young patients with otherwise unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy and characteristic cardiac magnetic resonance findings. Early recognition is important to facilitate molecular confirmation, family screening and timely consideration of disease-specific management before irreversible organ damage develops.

title: Impact of low-voltage area burden and topological obstacles on atrial fibrillation recurrence after pulmonary vein antrum isolation
authors: JungMin Choi; Y. Go; Soonil Kwon; Kyung-Yeon Lee; Hyo‐Jeong Ahn; So-Ryoung Lee; Taehun Kim; Jung Chan Lee; Eue‐Keun Choi; Seil Oh
abstract: Background Topological obstacles (TOs), electrically isolated regions such as the mitral annulus and atrial scars, can provide reentry circuits in the left atrium. Their quantity and relationship with low-voltage area (LVA) burden may influence recurrent atrial fibrillation (AF), but this impact remains poorly understood. We aimed to investigate the association between TO count, LVA burden, and post-ablation AF recurrence in patients undergoing de novo AF ablation. Methods Patients were categorized by TO counts, identified using pulmonary vein antrum isolation lines and voltage maps. LVA burden (<0.5 mV) was quantified and grouped into quartiles. One-year AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) recurrence was evaluated across groups. Results Among 237 patients (mean age 62.4 ± 8.8 years; 27.0% female, paroxysmal AF 42.6%, follow-up 1.0 ± 0. years), the majority had an intermediate TO count (TO = 3, 75.9%). Patients with the lowest TO count (TO = 1, 5.5%) were significantly older, had higher CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc scores, worse echocardiographic parameters, and the highest mean LVA burden (36.6% ± 24.8%). AF/AT recurrence occurred in 35.4% of patients. Although recurrence rates were numerically higher in patients with extreme TO counts (TO = 1 or ≥4) and lower in those with intermediate counts (TO = 2 or 3), these differences were not statistically significant ( p = 0.433), and the TO group remained non-significantly associated with recurrence after multivariable adjustment for age, AF clinical type, left atrial diameter, left ventricular ejection fraction, CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score, and LVA burden. TO counts differed significantly across LVA burden quartiles ( p < 0.001), with the greatest variation observed in the group with the highest LVA burden. Dominant frequency and organization index showed no significant intergroup differences. Conclusion Patients with extreme TO counts (TO = 1 or ≥4) showed a numerically higher, although not statistically significant, trend toward post-ablation recurrence compared with those with intermediate counts. TO quantity varied significantly with LVA burden, suggesting that atrial substrate heterogeneity may influence AF recurrence patterns.

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Complex Cardiac Conditions: Prognostic Challenges and Management Strategies
authors: Ehsan Shahverdi; Amin Shahverdi; Shadi Kamali
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is increasingly encountered in patients with complex cardiac conditions. In these populations, AF is associated with a higher risk of adverse outcomes, including stroke, heart failure progression, and mortality, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This chapter aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the pathophysiology, prognostic implications, and management strategies of AF in complex cardiac conditions. A narrative review approach was employed, integrating current evidence from clinical guidelines, major trials, and recent literature on AF in conditions such as, heart failure, valvular heart disease, congenital heart disease, and cardiomyopathies. Atrial fibrillation in complex cardiac conditions is driven by a multifactorial interplay of structural and electrical remodeling, neurohormonal activation, inflammation, and trigger activity. These mechanisms contribute to increased AF burden, disease progression, and reduced response to conventional therapies. Standard risk stratification tools have limitations in these populations, necessitating more individualized approaches. Management strategies, including anticoagulation, rate and rhythm control, and catheter ablation, often require adaptation to account for anatomical complexity and comorbidities. Atrial fibrillation in complex cardiac conditions represents a high-risk clinical entity requiring a comprehensive, individualized, and multidisciplinary management approach. Advances in imaging, digital health, and emerging therapies offer promising opportunities to improve patient outcomes.

title: The Temporal Investigation of Multimodal Elements (TIME) Study: protocol for an observational, longitudinal study to characterize the dynamic structure of molecular and digital data in older adults in stable health
authors: James T. Yurkovich; Emma Glass; Audrey N. Nash; Noah Levine; Sophia Lee; Katheryn Ehlen; Eduardo Hernandez; Prabin Gharti; Chatura Senadheera; Ashen Fernando; Drew Witherington; Lance T. Pflieger; Jyotika Erram; Noa Rappaport; Alison Le; John C. Newman; Brianna J. Stubbs
abstract: Background Biological systems exhibit dynamic patterns over multiple temporal scales—from minutes to months—that are poorly captured by conventional cross-sectional or low-frequency longitudinal studies. These patterns, including diurnal variations and underlying continuous rhythms, may be critical determinants of health, resilience, and disease risk in aging. Existing longitudinal studies in older adults lack high-frequency, multimodal measurements that integrate molecular, physiological, and digital health data streams. Objectives The TIME Study aims to: (i) Characterize temporal patterns in molecular, physiological, and digital health measures in healthy older adults; (ii) determine how these patterns vary across biological domains and relate to each other; and (iii) assess how physiological systems respond to defined perturbations (oral glucose tolerance and maximal exercise). Methods TIME is a single-site, observational, longitudinal study enrolling up to 150 adults aged ≥55 years. Over an 11-week main phase, participants complete seven weekly low-frequency visits, two perturbation challenge visits, and two, two-day high-frequency sampling epochs. Biospecimens, clinical measures, cognitive and physical performance tests, and continuous digital health data are collected. Follow-up visits occur at 6 and 12 months. Expected impact By integrating multimodal, temporally resolved data, TIME will provide a foundational dataset for understanding the role of biological rhythms in aging and inform future precision health strategies. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07107386 , identifier NCT07107386.

title: Deep Learning for Automated Coronary Artery Calcium Scoring in Chest CTs
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is an established marker of coronary atherosclerotic burden and cardiovascular risk.Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy, agreement, and processing efficiency of deep-learning-based automated coronary artery calcium scoring compared with expert manual Agatston scoring.Methodology: This prospective diagnostic accuracy study was conducted at Abwa Medical College Faisalabad from June 2024 to June 2025 and included 210 adult patients undergoing non-contrast chest CT.Demographic and clinical information including age, gender, body mass index, smoking status, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, family history of cardiovascular disease, and previous cardiovascular history was recorded using a standardized data collection form.Results: The mean age of participants was 61.8 ± 10.4 years, and 128 (61.0%) were male.The mean manual CAC score was 238.6 ± 315.4 Agatston units compared with 231.9 ± 307.8 using automated scoring (p=0.184).The mean absolute difference was 18.7 ± 24.6 units.Automated and manual scores showed a very strong correlation (r=0.967;p<0.001) and excellent agreement (ICC=0.974,95% CI: 0.966-0.981).Automated scoring correctly classified 195 (92.9%) patients into the appropriate CAC risk category, with a weighted kappa of 0.904 (95% CI: 0.861-0.947;p<0.001).Conclusion: It is concluded that deep-learning-based automated CAC scoring demonstrates excellent agreement with expert manual Agatston scoring, high diagnostic accuracy, reliable risk-category classification, and substantially faster processing.

title: From Data to Decision: Interpretable and Reliable Heart Disease Risk Prediction.
authors: ANDREI IONUȚ SPÎNU; Renato Constantin Ivănescu; Raluca Christiana Dănciulescu; DANIEL-ROBERT STĂNESCU
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for accurate and clinically meaningful risk prediction tool. METHODOLOGY: A retrospective analysis was performed on a dataset of 918 patients with complete clinical information. The relationship between variables and disease presence were explored using correlation and dependence measure. To prediction was made using logistic regression, linear discriminant analysis, and generalized additive models. The performances were evaluated using cross-validation, discrimination metrics, and calibration analysis. RESULTS: Functional and exercise-related variables, particularly Oldpeak, maximum heart rate, chest pain type, and ST slope showed the strongest correlation with disease presence. All models achieved AUROC values higher than 0.91. Logistic regression and generalized additive models performed similarly, with no statistically significant difference between them. Calibration analysis showed a good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. CONCLUSION: Heart disease prediction can be achieved with high accuracy using clinically accessible variables and interpretable models. Our findings suggest that simpler approaches remain suitable for practical clinical applications, while preserving transparency and usability.
